# Site platform: Kubernetes, registry, ingress and certificates

Every hosted site runs the same platform. RKE2 is the Kubernetes the rest runs on. Software arrives as a signed offline bundle and is loaded into the site's own registry (Zot, or Harbor at larger sites), so nothing is pulled from the internet. Kyverno refuses any image that is not signed with your organization's key. HAProxy is the one entry point for people, and cert-manager issues every certificate from the site's own certificate authority.

Back to the [component catalogue](./index.md).

## image:docker.io/goharbor/harbor-core

**What it provides.** Harbor core API (HQ and large sites, second wave).

**Why it is needed.** Harbor's API: projects, access and the registry's audit log. Harbor is the registry for HQ and large sites (second wave); small sites use Zot and do not run it.

| Kind | Container image |
| Pinned version or digest | `v2.15.5@sha256:5644d353661de160aca165b61a04228bdbcacc9c622dac64900ad3ce9166cdef` |
| Architecture component | `image-registry` |
| Used in | `deploy/bundle/images.lock.json` |
| Scope | Runtime: it runs in the product |
| Licence | Apache-2.0 |
| Cryptography | Not a validated cryptographic module |
| Air gap | Works air-gapped once mirrored: the pinned digest in the site registry, carried with its signature by the offline bundle |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | CM-7, CM-14, SI-7, SR-4, SR-11, SC-13 |
| Security fixes | Re-pinned by hand in a reviewed change when upstream publishes a fixed release (watch the project's security advisories). No scan of this third-party image runs in CI yet; Phase 48 adds a scan of the bundle's images. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Image signatures are copied into the site registry beside the images and checked with your organization's cosign public key at import and again at admission.
- Go cryptography in these components is not FIPS-validated (a GOFIPS140 build is unverified); Phase 48 records the gap.
- Harbor has no documented FIPS build. The upstream image is built on Photon OS and carries no validated cryptographic module: it is conditional at Protected B (SC-13) until it is rebuilt on UBI 9 with the OpenSSL FIPS provider on a FIPS-mode host, or your organization's authorizing official accepts it.
- Trivy is off at air-gapped sites; Harbor is for HQ and large sites only (second wave).

## image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-cainjector

**What it provides.** cert-manager CA injector: writes CA bundles into webhook configurations.

## image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller

**What it provides.** cert-manager controller: issues and renews site certificates.

**Why it is needed.** Issues and renews every TLS certificate at the site from the site's own certificate authority, with no ACME or internet certificate authority. Without it certificates would be issued and rotated by hand, and an expired certificate would stop sign-in and sessions.

## image:reg.kyverno.io/kyverno/kyverno

**What it provides.** Kyverno 1.20.0 admission controller: refuses any image not signed with your organization's key (D-15, Decision 1).

**Why it is needed.** The admission controller that refuses to start any container image not signed with your organization's key. It is the second check after the import check, so an unsigned or swapped image cannot run even if it reaches the registry.

| Kind | Container image |

| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |

| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

- Image signatures are copied into the site registry beside the images and checked with your organization's cosign public key at import and again at admission.
- Go cryptography in these components is not FIPS-validated (a GOFIPS140 build is unverified); Phase 48 records the gap.

- The upstream image is not built on UBI 9 and carries no validated cryptographic module: it is conditional at Protected B (SC-13) until it is rebuilt on UBI 9 with the OpenSSL FIPS provider on a FIPS-mode host, or your organization's authorizing official accepts it.

## tool:rke2

**What it provides.** RKE2 1.37.2+rke2r1 release tarball, image archives (core and Canal) and the rke2-selinux RPM for the air-gapped tarball install.

**Why it is needed.** The Kubernetes every site runs, installed from the air-gap tarball in its FIPS build, with the CIS profile, an audit policy and secrets encryption. Every other site part runs on it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | Pinned tool |
| Pinned version or digest | `1.37.2+rke2r1 (sha256:0568f48d772c7feff7056062225d5ba82fb3f73ea7acaea63862fe601dae6d92)` |
| Architecture component | `rke2` |
| Used in | `compliance/ci/tool-pins.json` |
| Scope | Runtime: it runs in the product |
| Licence | Apache-2.0 |
| Cryptography | Not a validated cryptographic module |
| Air gap | Works air-gapped once mirrored: the RKE2 tarball, image archives and rke2-selinux RPM carried by the bundle; host packages from the site's own OS repository |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, AC-6, AU-2, AU-12, SC-8, SC-13, SC-28, SI-2, SR-11, AU-8, AU-8(1), SC-45, CP-9 |
| Security fixes | Bumped by hand in a reviewed change (compliance/ci/TOOLS.md): the new SHA-256 is compared with the publisher's checksum before the pin changes. No automated advisory feed for pinned tools. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Production sites run the RKE2 FIPS build with Canal as the only CNI (the only CNI RKE2 rebuilds for FIPS), on hosts in FIPS mode.
- RKE2 runs with profile: cis and the DISA STIG settings, an audit policy that records Theia Cloud resources at Request and Secrets at Metadata only, and secrets-encryption on.
- k3s is for the lab and demos only and never appears in production values (D-14).
- SUSE documents the FIPS build on BoringCrypto (CMVP certificate 4968); that the certificate covers this 1.37 build in its operating environment is not yet confirmed, so the crypto stays unvalidated here.
- Every node and the import host run chrony from the site's own OS repository, configured only with the site's on-site authoritative time source (a GNSS-disciplined NTP appliance or a stratum-1 server). The node install refuses a clock that is unsynchronised, on its local clock, or beyond time.maxClockErrorMs (D-71, 47-22).
- The server token, which any etcd restore needs, and the secrets-encryption configuration are escrowed on custody media held by two key custodians apart from the backups; escrow-node.sh check finds a stale escrow after a rotation (D-73, 47-25).
